item.description: A Shas campaign video showing one son serving in the IDF and another studying in yeshiva sparks sharp online reactions, with users pointing to the party’s push for haredi draft exemptions.

item.title: Ben-Gvir: Two of three killed in Silwan clashes threw stones, firebombs and were shot by police
item.description:
National Security Minister Itamar Ben Gvir claimed that two of the three people reported killed overnight during criminal clashes in Jerusalem's Silwan neighborhood had thrown stones and firebombs and were shot by police during the incident.
He said that portraying them as “murder victims" amounts to “social engineering."

item.title: Concern in Israel: Hamas is pressuring the mediators
item.description: Hamas is pressuring mediators to issue a statement against Israel. Security forces express concern over kites sent toward the Gaza border.

item.title: Israel's secret channel to quell the tensions with Turkey
item.description: Israeli defense official says Israel does not seek conflict with Turkey but will act to prevent Turkish military systems in Syria from threatening Israel.

item.title: Rabbi Shmuel Eliyahu warns: 'Stay away from the Yanuka'
item.description: Rabbi Shmuel Eliyahu criticizes the Yanuka and the enthusiasm surrounding him, arguing that he is unlike the Baba Sali and other righteous figures he knew.

item.title: VP Vance is actually a dangerous choice for POTUS
item.description: The Vice President’s words and actions--the hard evidence--are what makes him a dangerous choice for President of the United States. Opinion.

item.title: Beyond the classroom: How schools shape the generation fighting for Israel
item.description: Education prioritizes responsibility over self-interest, connects learning to lived action and insists that Torah is not just something to study, but something to live.

item.title: Toronto man charged after alleged break-in at synagogue
item.description: Toronto man charged after allegedly breaking into a North York synagogue and stealing religious items. Police later recovered the items.

item.title: Iran warns US allies: 'Do not join' Trump's economic war
item.description: Iran warns countries against joining Trump's economic campaign, threatening confrontation and saying the Strait of Hormuz will remain closed.

item.title: Report: IDF carried out early morning strike in southern Lebanon
item.description:
Lebanese media reported that the IDF carried out an early morning strike in southern Lebanon.
According to the report, the strike took place in the Ali Taher ridge area.

item.title: Israel concerned over military escalation with Turkey
item.description: Israel’s defense establishment is closely monitoring the public exchange of threats between Jerusalem and Ankara, warning that tensions could undermine the IDF’s freedom of action in Syria.

item.title: Report: Iran-linked hackers shut down UK power plant
item.description: The Telegraph reports that Iran-linked hackers shut down a small British power plant for four days in an unprecedented cyberattack.

item.title: Tens of thousands at Western Wall Selichot as hostage survivors join prayer
item.description: Tens of thousands attend Selichot service at the Western Wall, joined by hostage survivors who recite a special prayer of thanksgiving for their return.

item.title: Why Israel is moving attack helicopters north
item.description: Following an Air Force investigation into the October 7 massacre, Squadron 190 has relocated north as the IDF seeks faster response times and greater readiness along Israel’s northern border.

item.description: The rise of the Democratic Socialists of America and its alliance with Radical Islam. Opinion.

item.title: “Loser with a low I.Q.:" Trump opens new front against Tucker Carlson
item.description: US President Donald Trump has opened a new front against conservative media personality Tucker Carlson and former members of Congress Marjorie Taylor Greene and Thomas Massie.

item.title: Firefighting crews battle blaze at vehicle lot in Kiryat Arba
item.description: Firefighting crews, together with the IDF, are operating at the scene. Police have blocked access routes. Heavy engineering equipment was brought into the flames to isolate vehicles that have not yet burned.

item.description: An experience is also a picture. You stand before it and gaze back at it, and the date is in the past.

item.title: PM congratulates Israeli gold medalist
item.description: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, this evening send congratulations to Artem Dolgopyat for his gold medal in the European gymnastics championship. “Congratulations to the three-time European Gymnastics Championship floor exercise champion, Artem Dolgopyat. Artem, you bring immense honor and national pride to the State of Israel, time and time again."

item.title: Paramount accuses Mark Ruffalo of using antisemitic tropes
item.description: Paramount Pictures accuses Hulk actor of using antisemitic tropes after he attacks the Ellison family and Israel in a rant against the planned merger with Warner Brothers.

item.title: Airport union chief warns Ben Gurion chaos could return
item.description: Ben Gurion Airport could face renewed disruptions as Israel Airports Authority union chairman Pinchas Idan refuses to guarantee the crisis is over and blames management for the airport’s manpower shortage.

item.title: Man collapses on Ashkelon beach
item.description: A man in his 70s collapsed during a sporting activity near Delilah Beach in Ashkelon. The MDA provided medical treatment and performed CPR, as well as defibrillating him. His pulse returned, and he was evacuated to Barzlai Hospital.

item.title: IDF eliminates Hamas officer in Gaza
item.description:
The IDF eliminated the terrorist Sharif al-Hasanat, a company commander in the military wing of Hamas earlier today in the Deir al-Balah area .
"The terrorist posed an immediate threat to our forces. Throughout the war, the terrorist took part in the restoration of Hamas' underground infrastructure. Recenly, he continued to try to promote terror against IDF forces and Israeli citizens," the IDF claimed.

item.title: Four kites found near Gaza border
item.description: At least seven kites have been found in the Gaza border area since October 7. The IDF has not yet determined that they originated in the Gaza Strip, but regional councils are demanding a real-time response.

item.title: Ben-Gurion Airport sounds alarm ahead of holiday rush
item.description: The Israel Airports Authority workers' committee warns that there is a shortage of between 400 and 500 workers in all departments. According to him, the shortage directly affects the service to passengers and is likely to be felt especially during the holiday rush.

item.title: UAL announces list for elections
item.description:
The 28th national conference of the United Arab List, held in Tayibe, has chosen the party list for the upcoming elections. Mansour Abbas was elected first, and will head the list.
After him, in order, were elected Walid Taha, Waleed Khalil Alhwashla, Iman Khatib-Yassin (in the fourth place, reserved for women), and Yasir Hujeirat.
